## Summary of the Analysis Approach

*to be completed together after choosing the primary analysis (max 100 words)*

We chose an individual-level analysis rather than a meta-analysis because all observations originated from a shared dataset, allowing us to retain participant-level information and account for institutional differences directly, without relying on potentially unstable effect-size estimates from institutions with small sample sizes. *!!! WE NEED TO MAKE SURE OUR FINAL ANALYSIS ACTUALLY ACCOUNTS FOR INSTITUTIONAL DIFFERENCES !!!!*

## Details of the Analysis

### Data Preparation and Participant Exclusions

#### Initial Inspection and Grade Availability

The SMARVUS dataset contained 12,570 observations and 788 variables. We checked for identical rows and missing or duplicated participant identifiers ('unique_id'); none were found. Missing reponses were investigated with reference to the variables required for this analysis rather than excluding participants with missing entries in other places of the questionnaire. Statistics attainment was recorded in 'grade', with 1820 participants having a grade entry other than 'NA' or '"Not Available"'.

```{r initial data inspection, include=FALSE}

# Initial dataset inspection
data_summary <- tibble(
  Observations = nrow(smarvus_raw),
  Variables = ncol(smarvus_raw),
  Duplicate_rows = sum(duplicated(smarvus_raw)),
  Duplicate_IDs = sum(duplicated(smarvus_raw$unique_id)),
  Missing_IDs = sum(is.na(smarvus_raw$unique_id))
)

data_summary
```



```{r recorded-grades, include=FALSE}

# Participants with recorded grades
smarvus_grades <- smarvus_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade), grade != "Not Available")

nrow(smarvus_grades)
```

#### Standarising Attainment Across Institutions


Reported grades were recorded differently across the participating surveys. This included different numerical scales, letter grades and ordinal categories. We examined each institutions lowest and highest documented grades before we constructed a comparable attainment variable. Supported numerical marks (0--100, 0--20, 0--10 and 1--10) were linearly rescaled to a common 0--100 range:

\[
\text{Scaled grade} = 100\,\frac{\text{Observed grade} - \text{Lowest possible grade}}{\text{Highest possible grade} - \text{Lowest possible grade}}.
\]

To keep observations that used letter grades, we used the midpoint of the applicable institution-specific percentage band as an *estimated* numerical mark. Grade categories that could not be converted reasonably or defensibly, including the 1--5 ordinal systems, ambiguous entries and values outside continuous-attainment datasets. This left us with 1362 converted numerical grades and 320 estimated letter grades (1662 observations in total). Grade-band midpoints are approximations, and it is important to note than converting to a common range does not remove the differences in grading standards across different institutions.




```{r grade-systems, include=FALSE}
# Compare grading systems across surveys
grade_summary <- smarvus_grades %>%
  group_by(country, survey_id, grade_low, grade_high) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Example_grades = paste(head(unique(grade), 3),
                           collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

print(n=22, grade_summary)
```

```{r grade-boundaries, include=FALSE}
# Institution-specific letter grade boundaries

grade_boundaries <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    survey_id = "brawijaya",
    grade = c("A", "B+", "B", "C+", "C", "D+", "D", "E"),
    lower = c(80, 75, 69, 60, 55, 50, 44, 0),
    upper = c(100, 80, 75, 69, 60, 55, 50, 44)
  ),

  tibble(
    survey_id = "york_can",
    grade = c("A+", "A", "B+", "B", "C+", "C", "D+", "D", "E", "F"),
    lower = c(90, 80, 75, 70, 65, 60, 55, 50, 40, 0),
    upper = c(100, 89, 79, 74, 69, 64, 59, 54, 49, 39)
  ),

  tibble(
    survey_id = "mef",
    grade = c("A", "A-", "B+", "B", "B-", "C+", "C", "C-", "D+", "D", "F"),
    lower = c(90, 80, 75, 70, 65, 60, 55, 50, 45, 35, 0),
    upper = c(100, 89, 79, 74, 69, 64, 59, 54, 49, 44, 35)
  ),

  tibble(
    survey_id = "limerick",
    grade = c("A1", "A2", "B1", "B2", "B3", "C1", "C2", "C3", "D1", "D2", "F"),
    lower = c(80, 75, 70, 65, 60, 55, 50, 45, 40, 35, 0),
    upper = c(100, 79, 74, 69, 64, 59, 54, 49, 44, 39, 35)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    grade_midpoint = (lower + upper) / 2
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(grade_boundaries[c("survey_id", "grade")]))


```



```{r prepare-grades, include=FALSE}
# Prepare numerical grades
smarvus_prepared <- smarvus_raw %>%
  mutate(
    
    grade_clean = str_trim(grade),
    
    # Convert numbers stored as text
    grade_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(str_remove(grade_clean, "%$"))),
    grade_low_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grade_low)),
    grade_high_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grade_high)),

    # Identify supported numerical grading systems
    supported_numeric =
      (grade_low_num == 0 & grade_high_num %in% c(10, 20, 100)) |
      (grade_low_num == 1 & grade_high_num == 10),

    # Check that marks are within their grading range
    valid_numeric =
      supported_numeric &
      !is.na(grade_num) &
      grade_num >= grade_low_num &
      grade_num <= grade_high_num) %>%

  # Add letter-grade midpoint conversions
  left_join(
    grade_boundaries %>%
      select(survey_id, grade, grade_midpoint),
    by = c("survey_id", "grade_clean" = "grade")) %>%

  # Create a single attainment variable
  mutate(
    grade_scaled = coalesce(
      if_else(valid_numeric,
        100 * (grade_num - grade_low_num) / (grade_high_num - grade_low_num),
        NA_real_),
      grade_midpoint),

    grade_method = case_when(
      !is.na(grade_midpoint) ~ "Letter grade midpoint",
      !is.na(grade_scaled) ~ "Numerical conversion",
      TRUE ~ "Unresolved or unavailable"))

# Check conversion results
smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade_clean), grade_clean != "Not Available") %>%
  count(grade_method)
```

```{r unresolved-grades, include=FALSE}
# Inspect observations without a usable converted grade
smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(grade_clean),
    grade_clean != "Not Available",
    is.na(grade_scaled)
  ) %>%
  
  count(survey_id, grade_clean, sort = TRUE)
```

#### Attention Checks and Exclusion Criteria


We assessed response quality using the six attention check items and the 'attention_amnesty' response. Participants were excluded if they answered at least one administered check incorrectly or explicitly selected '"No"' to the amnesty question. Missing check or amnesty responses were **not** interpreted as failures as the questions were not necessarily recorded for every survey. Under these rules, 1542 participants remained after attainment and quality screening. This is the *data-preparation sample*, not necessarily the final analysis sample: the anxiety-scale completeness criteria will be applied subsequently.

```{r attention-checks, include=FALSE}
# Attention check variables
check_cols <- c(
  "Q7.1_24",
  "Q8.1_21",
  "Q9.1_22",
  "Q11.1_9",
  "Q13.1_17",
  "Q15.1_9"
)

# Count checks answered
smarvus_prepared$n_checks_answered <-
  rowSums(!is.na(smarvus_prepared[, check_cols]))

# Count incorrect responses to answered checks
smarvus_prepared <- smarvus_prepared %>%
  mutate(
    n_checks_failed =
      as.integer(!is.na(Q7.1_24) & Q7.1_24 != 1) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q8.1_21) & Q8.1_21 != 5) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q9.1_22) & Q9.1_22 != 1) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q11.1_9) & Q11.1_9 != 3) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q13.1_17) & Q13.1_17 != 2) +
      as.integer(!is.na(Q15.1_9) & Q15.1_9 != 4)
  )

# Summarise attention check results for usable grades
smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade_scaled)) %>%
  count(n_checks_answered, n_checks_failed)

```

```{r participant-exclusions, include=FALSE}
# Participants with usable attainment
valid_grades <- smarvus_prepared %>%
  filter(!is.na(grade_scaled))

# Exclude explicit amnesty refusals
amnesty_passed <- valid_grades %>%
  filter(
    is.na(attention_amnesty) |
      attention_amnesty != "No")

# Exclude incorrect answered attention checks
smarvus_clean <- amnesty_passed %>%
  filter(n_checks_failed == 0)
```

The participant counts at each stage are summarised in the table below. Of the 1542 kept observations, 165 had no recorded attention check answers and 70 had a missing amnesty response. So, the conclusions should be checked for the sensitivity to the treatment of missing quality information. Results could also depend on if the estimated letter grades are included.

```{r exclusion-table, echo=FALSE}
exclusion_flow <- tibble(
  Stage = c(
    "Original dataset",
    "Non-missing grade entries",
    "Usable standardised attainment",
    "After attention amnesty",
    "After attention checks"
  ),

  N = c(
    nrow(smarvus_raw),
    nrow(smarvus_grades),
    nrow(valid_grades),
    nrow(amnesty_passed),
    nrow(smarvus_clean)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Excluded = lag(N) - N
  )

knitr::kable(exclusion_flow)
```

```{r validation-export, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled),
  all(is.finite(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled)),
  all(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled >= 0),
  all(smarvus_clean$grade_scaled <= 100),
  all(smarvus_clean$n_checks_failed == 0),
  n_distinct(smarvus_clean$unique_id) == nrow(smarvus_clean)
)

write_csv(smarvus_clean, "smarvus_clean.csv")
write_csv(exclusion_flow, "exclusion_flow.csv")
```


### Anxiety measures and scoring

Start by looking at the missing entries for the 4 different style of statistic and maths anxiety testing. 

```{r check-entries, include=FALSE}

stars_items   <- smarvus_clean %>% select(Q7.1_1:Q7.1_23)
rmars_s_items <- smarvus_clean %>% select(Q7.2_1:Q7.2_23)
stars_m_items <- smarvus_clean %>% select(Q8.1_1:Q8.1_20)
rmars_items   <- smarvus_clean %>% select(Q8.2_1:Q8.2_24)

stars_na   <- rowSums(is.na(stars_items))
rmars_s_na <- rowSums(is.na(rmars_s_items))
stars_m_na <- rowSums(is.na(stars_m_items))
rmars_na   <- rowSums(is.na(rmars_items))

missing_summary <- tibble(
  Scale = c("STARS (Stats)", "RMARS-S (Stats)", "STARS-M (Maths)", "RMARS (Maths)"),
  Items = c(ncol(stars_items), ncol(rmars_s_items), ncol(stars_m_items), ncol(rmars_items)),
  No_Missing_Answers = c(sum(stars_na == 0), sum(rmars_s_na == 0), sum(stars_m_na == 0), sum(rmars_na == 0)),
  
  # number who skipped some questions (at least 1 missing, but not all)
  Partial_Missing_N = c(
    sum(stars_na > 0 & stars_na < 23),
    sum(rmars_s_na > 0 & rmars_s_na < 23),
    sum(stars_m_na > 0 & stars_m_na < 20),
    sum(rmars_na > 0 & rmars_na < 24)
  ),
  
  # number who skipped every question
  All_Missing_N = c(sum(stars_na == 23), sum(rmars_s_na == 23), sum(stars_m_na == 20), sum(rmars_na == 24)),
  
  Min_Val = c(
    min(stars_items, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(rmars_s_items, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(stars_m_items, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(rmars_items, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  Max_Val = c(
    max(stars_items, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(rmars_s_items, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(stars_m_items, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(rmars_items, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

# Print nicely as a table
knitr::kable(missing_summary)

```

Found that majority of them have complete entries but some (especially RMARS and RMARS-S) have partially missing entries. so some students answered some of the questions for that test but not all. And 14-17 students missed all the questions. hence they will be removed.

We Investigated further into the partial missing entries, to see if there was a pattern.

```{r check-missing-entries, include=FALSE}

partial_data <- tibble(
  `STARS`   = stars_na,
  `RMARS-S` = rmars_s_na,
  `STARS-M` = stars_m_na,
  `RMARS`   = rmars_na
) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Scale", values_to = "Missing_Items") %>%
  # Keep only partially missing people (at least 1 missing, but not the entire scale)
  filter(
    Missing_Items > 0,
    !(Scale == "STARS"   & Missing_Items == 23),
    !(Scale == "RMARS-S" & Missing_Items == 23),
    !(Scale == "STARS-M" & Missing_Items == 20),
    !(Scale == "RMARS"   & Missing_Items == 24)
  )

# Plot a separate bar chart for each scale using facet_wrap()
# factor(Missing_Items) makes R treat each numberggplot(partial_data, aes(x = factor(Missing_Items))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ Scale, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title = "Items Skipped by Partially Missing Participants",
    x = "Number of Missing Items",
    y = "Number of Participants"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() as a clean category on the x-axis


# Check which universities have people missing exactly 4 items
smarvus_clean %>%
  mutate(rmars_s_na = rowSums(is.na(select(., Q7.2_1:Q7.2_23)))) %>%
  filter(rmars_s_na == 4) %>%
  count(university, sort = TRUE)

smarvus_clean %>%
  mutate(rmars_na = rowSums(is.na(select(., Q8.2_1:Q8.2_24)))) %>%
  filter(rmars_na == 4) %>%
  count(university, sort = TRUE)

# Check which specific RMARS-S questions have the most missing values
# colSums(is.na(...)) counts the NAs in each COLUMN (each question)
colSums(is.na(rmars_s_items)) %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% head(6)

# 3. Do the same quick check for RMARS (maths)
colSums(is.na(rmars_items)) %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% head(6)

```
From the bar chart we can see that in RMARS and RMARS-S, majority of students who missed questions, missed exactly 4 questions. which led us to see if these were the same 4 questions. These exactly 4 missing all came from the same university (Erasmus University Rotterdam), and all these students had not completed the last 4 questions on the RMARS and RMARS-S surveys. 


```{r Rotterdam, include=FALSE}
rotterdam <- smarvus_clean %>%
  filter(university == "Erasmus University Rotterdam")

nrow(rotterdam)

rotterdam %>%
  mutate(rmars_s_na = rowSums(is.na(select(., Q7.2_1:Q7.2_23)))) %>%
  count(rmars_s_na)

rotterdam %>%
  mutate(rmars_na = rowSums(is.na(select(., Q8.2_1:Q8.2_24)))) %>%
  count(rmars_na)

rotterdam %>%
  select(Q7.2_20:Q7.2_23, Q8.2_21:Q8.2_24) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(!is.na(.))))

```

None of the Rotterdam participants (77) answered the last 4 questions of the RMARS-S and RMARS questions, suggesting they weren't available on their survey. 

```{r Other_Missing_entries, include=FALSE}

# 1. Check if any single STARS or STARS-M question has noticeably more NAs than the rest
# (Since 14-17 people missed the whole scale, random 1-item skips should only push numbers to ~15-19)
colSums(is.na(stars_items)) %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% head(5)
colSums(is.na(stars_m_items)) %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% head(5)

# 2. Check who missed the ENTIRE STARS or STARS-M scale
# Note: the "|" symbol means "OR"
smarvus_clean %>%
  mutate(
    stars_all_na   = rowSums(is.na(select(., Q7.1_1:Q7.1_23))) == 23,
    stars_m_all_na = rowSums(is.na(select(., Q8.1_1:Q8.1_20))) == 20
  ) %>%
  filter(stars_all_na | stars_m_all_na) %>%
  count(university, stars_all_na, stars_m_all_na)


```
